mechanism_narrative: The four-week upward trend in RETAIL_REC and TRANSIT reflects easing mobility constraints; continued improvement in these co-moving activity series will lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -44.9 at t-3w to -36.4 at t-0w
fact:TRANSIT rose from -66.7 at t-3w to -62.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is less than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days despite the prior four-week upward trend in RETAIL_REC and TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery and pharmacy mobility crossing above -10 percent signals that essential-errand restrictions have eased enough to normalize routines, which spills over into discretionary retail and lifts RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -10 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -15.3 at t-3w to -6.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: After GROCERY_PHARM crosses above -10, mean RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days is not higher than the prior 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Transit and workplace recovery interact: returning commuters and office workers create weekday footfall that disproportionately benefits retail and recreation, so joint improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES predicts higher RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 3 points and WORKPLACES improves by more than 3 points from t-3w to t-0w
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose 4.0 points and WORKPLACES rose 4.6 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: When both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve by more than 3 points over four weeks, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the preceding 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Falling RESIDENTIAL mobility means fewer people are staying home; in the current reopening regime this release from home confinement drives discretionary trips and raises RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 18 percent above baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 20.0 at t-3w to 17.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: When RESIDENTIAL falls below 18 percent above baseline, RETAIL_REC mean over the next 14 days is not higher than the prior 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: As PARKS mobility recovers, outdoor recreation substitutes for indoor retail-and-recreation trips, diverting discretionary time and spend away from RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -35 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS was -39.9 at t-0w after -41.3 at t-1w
failure_condition: When PARKS rises above -35 percent, RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is higher than or equal to the previous 7-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Workplace and transit mobility remain far below baseline, indicating work-from-home policies still cap weekday retail demand; as these policy-sensitive series improve slowly, RETAIL_REC rises but only if they stay above their recent lows.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains above -40 percent and TRANSIT remains above -65 percent from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -35.1 and TRANSIT at -62.7 at t-0w are above their t-3w levels
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain above these thresholds, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the preceding 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The rapid normalization of GROCERY_PHARM from panic-level lows reduces stockpiling and frees household budgets for discretionary retail, lifting RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM improves by more than 3 points over two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -15.4 at t-2w to -6.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: When GROCERY_PHARM improves by more than 3 points over two weeks, RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is not higher than the prior 7-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Residential and parks mobility jointly indicate a shift from home confinement to outdoor activity; when RESIDENTIAL falls while PARKS rises, retail-and-recreation trips increase over two weeks as households expand their activity radius.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by at least 1 point and PARKS rises by at least 1 point from t-1w to t-0w
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 18.7 at t-1w to 17.6 at t-0w
fact:PARKS rose from -41.3 at t-1w to -39.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: When RESIDENTIAL falls and PARKS rises from t-1w to t-0w, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than the prior 14-day mean.
